author: Joey Holmes
citation: Within 20 minutes of hitting the coast, we had found ourselves a delightful little east-facing beach looking across the stillness of the Argolic Gulf. The barely audible lapping of the waves and slow rising of the huge orange full moon immediately soothed us into a deep and satisfying sleep. Nothing but the rising of the sun at our feet to wake us.
location: Remote beaches on the Peloponnese Peninsula, Greece (including near Argolic Gulf, Stoupa, Skoutari)
provenance: Personal account by Joey Holmes (Cool of the Wild / Mapping Megan), published around 2016, of a week of wild camping without a tent (bivvy/sleeping bag on sand or pebbles) on deserted beaches in the Peloponnese, early May, multiple nights directly on the shore.
